![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/90d15521c8aa8ef53e0659debffdb85010332cd8ba653ca52b6e36a40a05b57a.png)

Use the model above to determine the missing fraction in the following division problem.

$$
4÷\frac{7}{8}=4\,\frac{\boxed{\,\,}}{\boxed{\,\,}}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let's start by interpreting our model:

- The model shows $4$ wholes split into eighths.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/a216109fd3b33a037b060dc832e208e2d2162d5a13b405a2a06b39e5f6656668.png)

- There are $7$ eighths in each group, with $4$ remaining.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/7a3a4edb355d0c6fd7138dcfe56c420a4a52faeff12d12437d4b152294e6283e.png)

Note the following: 

- There are $4$ full groups.

- There are $4$ eighths left over out of a possible group of $7.$ So the fractional part of our answer is 

$$
\frac{4}{7}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
4÷\frac{7}{8}=4\,\frac{4}{7}.
$$
